main_text.l: Artificum dedit esse dextra? Sic docta (dicit Caelituum Deus) Proles Isaci me petet unicum, Jovamque me professa solum, Sacra procul peregrina pellet, Divosque fictos. Namque necessitas Invisa lethi diripit omnia Me sic jubente: & cuncta nostris Arbitriis animata viuunt.
Infligo cunctis vulnera plebibus, Cladesque diras: sed mala quae facit Tristésve plagas sola fortis Nostra valet medicare dextra.
Quasi superbas perdere destinet Gentes: quis illas fortior adiuuet, Seruetque vindex? Quisve certis Eripiat potior periclis?
Vos alta testor sydera: Olympicae Vos testor arces, Imperiis rego Qui cuncta summis: cuique nulla Saecla ferunt peritura finem,
Quid? Ense stricto si meditor meos Infensus hostes perdere funditus: Et me per horrendas acerba Terribilem rapit ira caedes:
O, quam furenti verbere puniam Invisa iudex crimina gentium, Qua Numen oderunt supremum

page.notes: Lines are verse; each stanza is given as one paragraph, with the line breaks shown as spaces. Long s is written as plain s throughout. The i/j and u/v spelling has been normalised (Iouamque as Jovamque, Inuisa as Invisa, and so on). The word "Qua" at the end of the last line and the Greek-style marks at the start of some lines were not transcribed as letters. The word "Quasi" in the fourth-to-last stanza is read as printed "Quasi" [?], and the printed word "Qui" in the fourth stanza is uncertain [?]. The first line of the page starts with a small decorative mark, which is not a letter.
